evidence: Ter. Ph. 454: quot hominēs, tot sententiae
Cic. Att. 7.13a.3: vir meā sententiā magnus
terms.comment: In my opinion: meā sententiā (Cic. Att. 7.13a.3; Traupman 21, 354) or meā quidem sententiā (Cic. de Or. 1.20). To give one’s opinion: sententiam dīcere (Traupman 177, 354). “What’s your opinion?” is quid tibi vidētur? or quid cēnsēs? (see seem, think).

terms.gloss: a belief, an impression, what one supposes (often against the facts); expectation; reputation
evidence: Sen. Ep. 13.4: saepius opīniōne quam rē labōrāmus
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “opinion, supposition, conjecture, imagination, fancy, belief”. Ut opīniō mea fert, as I believe (Cic. Fam. 1.9.22); opīniōne celerius, sooner than expected; and the opinion others hold of someone, his reputation.

phrases.latin: Quot hominēs, tot sententiae; suus cuique mōs.
phrases.english: So many men, so many opinions; everyone has his own way.
Labienus, a great man in my opinion
we suffer more often from what we imagine than from what is
